locator: The left-hand frame: a young woman at a kitchen table holding up a pie, a man in evening dress in the doorway behind, both at about three metres, full length.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1903. Used only as a reference picture people are judged against and as the cut of the 1904 working dress (T-3423); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-06 (T-3423) from the master TIFF. A young woman in a pale shirtwaist with a white standing collar and a dark tie, sleeves full at the shoulder and pushed up at the forearm; a white bib apron with ruffled shoulder straps over it, tied at the waist and reaching below the knee; a dark full skirt to the floor with flounces near the hem; low dark shoes; hair swept up all round into a full knot on top, with a white cap pinned to it. The tile wainscot, clock shelf and table are a studio kitchen set. A staged studio photograph, not of Chicago or of any named servant.
note: One of the 1904 working-woman reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/working_woman_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: how a working woman's shirtwaist, bib apron and long dark skirt hang on a standing figure at a few metres
the swept-up hair of the decade, and how high the knot sits
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Martha Williamson; no likeness is asserted
